item.title: Columbia County man accused of raping, recording sleeping woman sentenced
item.description: A Columbia County man who assaulted a woman and recorded it while she was sleeping has been sentenced to three years in prison. The post Columbia County man accused of raping, recording sleeping woman sentenced appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Manning uses arm and legs to lead No. 14 Texas to a 41-27 Citrus Bowl win over No. 18 Michigan
item.description: Arch Manning made big plays with his arm and his legs Wednesday in the Citrus Bowl, throwing two touchdown passes and putting it away with a 60-yard scoring run in a 41-27 victory that ended a rough month for No. 14 Michigan. The post Manning uses arm and legs to lead No. 14 Texas to a 41-27 Citrus Bowl win over No. 18 Michigan appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Miami beats defending national champ Ohio State 24-14 in the CFP quarterfinal at Cotton Bowl
item.description: Keionte Scott returned an interception 72 yards for a touchdown, Carson Beck threw a scoring pass and No. 10 Miami shocked defending champion Ohio State 24-14 on Wednesday night at the Cotton Bowl in the first College Football Playoff quarterfinal. The post Miami beats defending national champ Ohio State 24-14 in the CFP quarterfinal at Cotton Bowl appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.description: The Augusta University women's basketball team defeated the Converse Valkyries 91–69 Wednesday at Christenberry Fieldhouse. The post Augusta University women’s basketball tops Converse 91–69 appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: 5-year-old girl killed after being struck by vehicle in Aiken front yard
item.description: A 5-year-old girl was tragically killed in Aiken on Wednesday afternoon when a car struck her while entering her front yard, authorities said. The post 5-year-old girl killed after being struck by vehicle in Aiken front yard appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Bill eliminates last minute ethics complaints in Georgia elections
item.description: A bill that takes effect Thursday bars Georgia's State Ethics Commission from investigating complaints filed 60 days or fewer before an election. The post Bill eliminates last minute ethics complaints in Georgia elections appeared first on The Augusta Press.
